fullPassage: Difficult as it may be to accept, many aspects of life are beyond your control. People often fall into the trap of trying to control too much or worrying excessively about potential disasters, which doesn’t really prevent adverse outcomes but only adds to stress. To avoid unnecessary anxiety, it is better to focus on aspects within your control. If, when faced with a worrying situation, you automatically tell yourself, “This is going to be horrible,” you may benefit from a different approach. Instead of panicking, ask yourself, “What is the most awful outcome, and how can I respond to it?” By considering the worst-case scenario and planning your response, you empower yourself to tackle challenges more effectively, and this can have the benefit of reassuring yourself that you are strong enough to handle them. On replay in many people’s heads are yesterday’s conversations, which can lead to an endless cycle of self-doubt and discouragement. If you’re dissatisfied with something that happened, remind yourself that mulling over the memory will not solve anything. Come up with a solution that will make you feel better, or failing that, do something that will distract you long enough to refocus your brain on something more productive. Finally, engaging in activities that naturally improve mood, such as exercising, eating well, and getting enough sleep, can significantly reduce stress and is all within your control.

① too weak(너무 약한) — 안심시킨다는 흐름과 반대
② afraid(두려워하는) — 자신감을 주는 맥락과 모순
③ strong enough(충분히 강한) ✅ 정답 — 도전을 감당할 만큼 강하다고 스스로를 안심시킴
④ unwilling(내키지 않는) — 문맥과 어울리지 않음
det.tip: empower·reassuring의 긍정적 맥락 → 도전을 감당할 만큼 strong enough(충분히 강한)

questions.passage: Difficult as it may be to accept, many aspects of life are beyond your control. People often fall into the trap of trying to control too much or worrying excessively about potential disasters, which doesn’t really prevent adverse outcomes but only adds to stress. To avoid unnecessary anxiety, it is better to focus on aspects within your control. If, when faced with a worrying situation, you automatically tell yourself, “This is going to be horrible,” you may benefit from a different approach. Instead of panicking, ask yourself, “What is the most awful outcome, and how can I respond to it?” By considering the worst-case scenario and planning your response, you empower yourself to tackle challenges more effectively, and this can have the benefit of reassuring yourself that you are strong enough to handle them. On replay in many people’s heads are yesterday’s conversations, which can lead to an endless cycle of self-doubt and discouragement. If you’re dissatisfied with something that happened, remind yourself that mulling over the memory will not solve anything. Come up with a solution that will make you feel better, or failing that, do something that will distract you long enough to refocus your brain on something more productive. Finally, engaging in activities that naturally improve mood, such as exercising, eating well, and getting enough sleep, can significantly reduce stress and is all within your control.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ④번은 원문과 불일치 — 기억을 곱씹는 것은 아무것도 해결하지 못한다고 했음

① 일치 — many aspects of life are beyond your control
② 일치 — worrying ... doesn't really prevent adverse outcomes but only adds to stress
③ 일치 — By considering the worst-case scenario and planning your response, you empower yourself to tackle challenges more effectively
④ 불일치 — 원문은 'mulling over the memory will not solve anything(곱씹어도 아무것도 해결 못 함)'이므로 '큰 도움이 된다'는 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: '해결하지 못한다'를 '큰 도움이 된다'로 뒤집는 정반대 오답 패턴에 유의

ch: 삶의 많은 부분은 우리의 통제를 벗어나 있다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ who → which (선행사가 사물인 conversations이므로 관계대명사 which를 써야 함)
det.analysis:
① ✅ 적절 — 명령문과 의문문 인용이 어법상 옳음
② ✅ 적절 — By + 동명사(considering) 및 병렬 구조가 올바름
③ ❌ 오류 — 관계대명사 who는 사람을 선행사로 받는데 여기서는 사물인 conversations를 받으므로 which가 되어야 함 ←정답
④ ✅ 적절 — 조건절 if + 현재시제, remind + 목적어 구조가 옳음
det.tip: 관계대명사: 사람 → who, 사물 → which. 선행사가 conversations(사물)이므로 which

det.tip: 동사를 수식 → 부사. automatic(형용사) → automatically(부사)

다음 우리말에 맞도록 조건에 주어진 단어를 모두 사용하여 빈칸에 알맞은 영어를 쓰시오. (영어로) 불필요한 불안을 피하려면, 자신이 통제할 수 있는 측면에 집중하는 것이 더 낫다. To avoid unnecessary anxiety, it is better to ______________________. (6단어)
